# Offline DNS regression workbench

Implement `submission/main.py` using the task instruction. The scaffold deliberately has no resolver or optimizer. The examples demonstrate synthesized wildcard CNAME answers, empty nonterminals, duplicate-insensitive observation comparison, timeouts, tied optimal bases, and loop-versus-budget precedence. `check_examples.py` accepts either tied optimum in the wildcard example.

Run `python3 check_examples.py` after implementing the submission. This checker is only a public sanity aid. The invalid example tests an empty profile list. Keep all runtime dependencies within the standard library or your submitted tree.

Research inspiration: [Eywa, NSDI 2026](https://www.usenix.org/conference/nsdi26/presentation/mondal), [official artifact](https://github.com/microsoft/Model_Based_Testing_Using_LLMs), [RFC 1034](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1034), and [RFC 4592](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4592). The fixtures and code here are newly authored, synthetic data. No upstream generated case, real resolver bug label, or real traffic is included. This task evaluates the explicit frozen local contract, not full DNS conformance or Eywa's LLM model-generation quality.
=== main.py ===
"""Public scaffold: implement the model and diagnostic selection here."""
import json
import sys


def analyze(document):
    """Return runs, audits and an exact minimum diagnostic basis."""
    raise NotImplementedError('Implement the contract in instruction.md')


def main():
    document = json.load(sys.stdin)
    result = analyze(document)
    print(json.dumps(result, separators=(',', ':')))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
